title: Stable FP8 on Hopper — calibration pipeline, monitoring, and automatic fallback
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Background: We want to enable FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) profiles for Hopper-class GPUs (H100 and derivatives) across hosted and Dedicated runtimes. Prior attempts produced intermittent accuracy regressions and rare instability (NaNs, outlier activations) on long-context and sparsely-activated models. This ticket implements a robust calibration pipeline, per-layer format selection heuristics, telemetry, and an automatic fallback policy to protect customers.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
- Deterministic calibration run for each model version producing a quantization profile artifact.
- Per-task accuracy delta vs FP32: perplexity <= +0.5% (LM), exact-match/ROUGE degradation <= 1% (downstream), embedding cosine similarity >= 0.995.
- 99th percentile latency impact <= +10% at production batch distributions.
- No NaNs/infs observed in 1000 synthetic long-context inference runs.
- Automatic fallback to INT8 or FP16 if production SLOs or quality gates are violated for >10 minutes.

Approach summary:
1) Calibration harness: build a reproducible harness that samples a representative batch distribution (batch-size, sequence-length histogram) pulled from anonymized production telemetry (controlled dataset in S3). Calibration computes per-layer activation ranges (min/max and 99.9th percentile), per-channel stats for weight tensors, and stores EMA-scaled ranges.
2) Format selector heuristic: compute dynamic_range_ratio = max_range / median_nonzero_range per layer. If dynamic_range_ratio < 8 => prefer E4M3 (better precision for small dynamic ranges). If >= 8 => prefer E5M2 (wider exponent range). Allow an override map for known sensitive ops (layernorm/softmax/quantile ops) to force E5M2. The selector also tags layers as 'guarded' if outlier incidence > 0.01% during calibration.
3) Stability fixes implemented in runtime:
   - Outlier clipping policy: per-inference clamp based on calibration percentiles with a tunable multiplier (default 3.0).
   - Loss-scaling check for FP8 accumulation paths and consistent max-abs tracking to avoid dynamic oscillation.
   - KV cache index alignment guard to prevent stale cache reads when mixed precision paths are activated.
   - NaN/inf fast-detect and local-recompute path that falls back only the current request to INT8/FP16, with circuit-breaker metrics.
4) Validation harness and metrics:
   - End-to-end regression suite with canonical prompts for LM/QA/Seq2Seq/embeddings.
   - Statistical tests (bootstrap) to assert against acceptance criteria.
   - Telemetry hooks: per-request quantization-profile-id, per-layer scale histograms, and per-request quality flags.
5) CI and stress tests: integrate into GPU CI pool with randomized seeds, batch distributions, and long-context (up to 32k tokens simulated by stress harness). Add perf bench capturing p50/p95/p99 and memory.
6) Canary and rollout plan:
   - Stage 0: internal Dedicated test cluster (zero customer traffic).
   - Stage 1: hosted API opt-in beta for select partners (1% traffic) for 48 hours.
   - Stage 2: progressive ramp 1% -> 10% -> 50% with automated rollback if any of the quality or SLO gates fail for longer than 10 minutes.

Calibration workflow (developer-facing):
- checkout runtime branch and run tools/calibrate_model --model <MODEL> --data-s3 s3://redwood-fixtures/fp8-calib/ --seed <N> --out artifacts/<model>-fp8-profile.json
- The tool emits: per-layer range CSV, recommended-format map (E4M3/E5M2), and confidence score.
- CI attaches profile to the model bundle and runs quantized regression.

Trade-offs and notes:
- We bias toward conservative selection (prefer E5M2) for ops historically brittle to exponent clipping (layernorm, softmax). This increases memory/perf slightly but reduces customer risk.
- Using a dynamic selector (per-layer) increases code-path complexity and test surface compared to a single global format; justified because mixed-format nets show >2x reduction in accuracy regressions in our benchmark.
- Calibration artifacts are non-sensitive but derived from sampled telemetry. We store only aggregated statistics and anonymized prompt ids.

Rollout/monitoring gates (automated):
- Quality gate: rolling 1-hour window median LM delta and downstream task delta must remain within targets.
- Perf gate: rolling 10-minute p99 latency must not exceed baseline by >10%.
- Error gate: any increase in NaN/inf or per-request failure rate > 0.05% triggers automatic rollback.

Next steps and owners:
- Calibration harness implementation (ENG): Ava Patel (owner) — ETA 2025-02-20.
- Runtime stability fixes (ENG): Kaito Wong — ETA 2025-02-28.
- Validation suite and metrics (QA/ML): Priya Srinivasan — ETA 2025-03-03.
- Canary rollout & monitoring alerts (SRE): Miguel Alvarez — ETA 2025-03-10.

Acceptance tests (manual/automated):
- run ci/quant-regression.sh against model family X with the new profile and verify metrics in artifacts/regression/<model>.json
- validate Grafana dashboard shows zero critical alerts and profile_id annotation on traces for 48h of canary traffic.

Fallback behavior (detailed):
- Local: for a single request that triggers NaN or scale overflow, attempt local recompute with INT8 fallback and mark the quantization-profile with a warning.
- Global: if a profile causes >0.05% errors or quality gate violation across a 10-minute window, promote automatic revert to the previous released profile and create ENG auto-revert ticket for postmortem.

Documentation and customer opt-in:
- Add a Console toggle per-organization to opt into 'experimental FP8' with clear risk description and link to the playbook. UI changes tracked in PM ticket PM-4112.
